#### What this PR does / why we need it:
The [E2E/Conformance test](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/master/test/e2e) process spawns pods in separate namespaces to run E2E/Conformance tests. If pods are referencing images from a private registry, the secrets wouldn’t be available in the newly created namespaces and the pod will fail to start.

The changes in this PR leverage the `--e2e-docker-config-file` flag which takes in a file containing the credentials that can be used to pull images from private registries, needed for a test. Before running the tests, the e2e framework [creates a test namespace](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/3e26e104bdf9d0dc3c4046d6350b93557c67f3f4/test/e2e/framework/framework.go#L418) for each of the tests. After creating the namespace, a secret is deployed in the new namespace.
With the Secret created, the default service account (in the new namespace) is patched with the created secret and can then be referenced by the test pod, and repository authentication should be successful.

issue_context.title: [E2E] Support for pulling images from private registry
issue_context.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Our team is using sonobuoy to run the conformance tests on a cluster. When running Sonobuoy E2E/Conformance tests, deployed pods will go into an ErrImagePull/ImagePullBackOff state when the image resides in a repository that requires authentication, and credentials are not passed with the request.

The [E2E/Conformance test](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/master/test/e2e) process spawns pods in separate namespaces to run E2E/Conformance tests. If pods are referencing images from a private registry, the secrets wouldn’t be available in the newly created namespaces and the pod will fail to start.

This is the issue reported by one of the sonobuoy users - https://github.com/vmware-tanzu/sonobuoy/issues/1038

Kubernetes E2E framework provides a `--e2e-docker-config-file`  flag which takes in a file containing the credentials that can be used to pull images from private registries needed for a test.  Using the credentials a secret can be created in the newly created namespace. 
With the Secret created, the default service account (in the new namespace) will be patched with the created secret and can then be referenced by the test pod, and repository authentication should be successful.


### Why is this needed?

As of now, when running the E2E tests, the flag is only being checked in a single test - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/57eb5d631ccd615cd161b6da36afc759af004b93/test/e2e/common/node/runtime.go#L292-L308
so despite passing the credential file, other tests would fail.

I´m not sure I understand well this issue, is the request to run the conformance tests being able to use a different registry than the one defined in the tests?

that was fixed by @smarterclayton here https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/93510

Or is this about some specific tests ?

The linked issue refers to the former https://github.com/vmware-tanzu/sonobuoy/issues/1038#issuecomment-563365850 and your fix is modifying the tests that verify pulling images from registries, that seems totally unrelated

I think that the request is that when users override  the e2e test images repository `KUBE_TEST_REPO=quay.io/openshift/community-e2e-images` , if this is authenticated, the e2e should still be able to work

> Our team is using sonobuoy to run the conformance tests on a cluster. When running Sonobuoy E2E/Conformance tests, deployed pods will go into an ErrImagePull/ImagePullBackOff state when the image resides in a repository that requires authentication, and credentials are not passed with the request.

@Divya063 can you provide more details about how you are running conformance tests? are you overriding the images repository with the `KUBE_TEST_REPO` env variable? or using some proxy or something unusual?
@dims it seems you have more context about this https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/109523#issuecomment-1100974649

copying here for visibility, so I wonder if we are not having the same mistake as the reported in the above issue

>> I edited a sonobuoy binary to set the KUBE_TEST_REPO=my/repo and got the following output. You can see most of the images were translated. The authenticated and invalid images were not.

> authenticated and invalid images are hard coded by design and won't be switched as they are testing special conditions (and just copying images are not enough)

sorry for the confusion, currently we are using `KUBE_TEST_REPO_LIST` env variable for overriding the images repositories. Through this, we can pass in the config having the registries mapping which may look like this:
```
buildImageRegistry: testbeta64.jfrog.io/docker-local
dockerGluster: docker.io/gluster
dockerLibraryRegistry: docker.io/library
e2eRegistry: testbeta64.jfrog.io/docker-local
e2eVolumeRegistry: gcr.io/kubernetes-e2e-test-images/volume
gcRegistry: testbeta64.jfrog.io/docker-local
gcEtcdRegistry: registry.k8s.io
promoterE2eRegistry: testbeta64.jfrog.io/docker-local
sigStorageRegistry: registry.k8s.io/sig-storage
gcAuthenticatedRegistry: testbeta64.jfrog.io/docker-local
```
so currently any tests whose image resides in the authenticated registry (here testbeta64.jfrog.io) fail as the pods spawned in the new namespace don't have credentials for the `testbeta64.jfrog.io` registry. In the current approach, I'm using --docker-config-file to pass in the credentials and after [the namespace is created](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/8ca843f037d55b8177f37bf91b951a7a09251a23/test/e2e/framework/framework.go#L452) for each test, a secret is created using the content present in the `docker-config-file` and is patched with the default service account. This way every new test namespace which is created would have access to the secret. 

cc @dims @aojea

@Divya063 yep, this is by design. Note that None of the conformance tests should fail in an air-gapped environment (no access to internet). We don't provide the same guarantee to the other e2e tests.

If you see test marked as conformance ( https://cs.k8s.io/?q=ConformanceIt&i=nope&files=&excludeFiles=&repos=kubernetes/kubernetes ) fail, then we can have this conversation.

My main concern is this:

- KUBE_TEST_REPO_LIST is a internal detail undocumented or at least not well documented
- the flag `"docker-config-file", "", "A file that contains credentials which can be used to pull images from certain private registries, needed for a test.")` is a flag for a test

Using a flag created for a test to provide a feature to an undocumented environment variable sounds wrong ... very wrong

In case that we see motivation to support this setup, and thinking out loud:
1. we perpetuate the env hack and add `KUBE_TEST_REPO_CONFIG_FILE`
2. we add new flags or another way to configure the repo list and the secret
- ...

What I definitely think we should not do is to reuse the existing flag

@spiffxp @BenTheElder

The KUBE_TEST_REPO_LIST variable is currently being used in sonobuoy to override the registries- https://github.com/vmware-tanzu/sonobuoy/blob/bd5465d6b2b2b92b517f4c6074008d22338ff509/cmd/sonobuoy/app/args.go#L561
yes, `KUBE_TEST_REPO_LIST` was designed ONLY for conformance.
I see, even for conformance the tests would fail (if the images the tests are using reside in a private registry) as currently there is no way to pass the secrets.

> yes, KUBE_TEST_REPO_LIST was designed ONLY for conformance.

It also got extended to work for CSI storage tests (pulling sidecars). Those storage tests are not and cannot be marked as conformance tests because they depend on optional features, but being able to run them for suitable clusters is useful nonetheless. Those clusters might be air-gappend and/or use registries which need authentication.

Actually... did we agree to rename this command line flag?

I don't see the value behind that. I would simply remove "e2e-docker-config-file" from this PR.
I think we agreed to leave the `--docker-config-file` flag as it is so the current users don't get impacted, and instead introduce a new flag for setting private registry credentials.
But those two now set the same field. So if someone uses `-e2e-docker-config-file`, they might as well just use `-docker-config-file` because it has the exact same effect?

The `--docker-config-file` is being used for an image pull test from an authenticated registry here - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/d004f324d3f5dc92f0baf2e6e176877e05471ab9/test/e2e/common/node/runtime.go#L293 
whereas the `--e2e-docker-config-file`  is being used to pass in the registry credentials so that it can be utilized by all the spawned e2e pods whose third-party images reside in an authenticated registry.
If the goal is to have two different flags with different meanings, then you need two separate fields in TestContext. Otherwise both flags have the exact same effect.

I'm using the field `E2EDockerConfigFile` for `--e2e-docker-config-file` flag https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/abba87da2e9b6b0bc33ec62d9f93aaac98edaa15/test/e2e/framework/test_context.go#L366
You are right of course. Not sure why I missed that, sorry.
